overview.description: Huutopussi (Finnish for 'Bidding Bag') is a prestigious Finnish trick-taking game for four players in partnerships. It is an evolution of 'Marjapussi', adding a complex bidding phase where partnerships compete for the right to exchange cards and set the contract. It is famous for its 'Marriage' system, where declaring a King-Queen pair of the same suit establishes the trump and awards points.

history.origins: Derived from the older game 'Marjapussi'. It includes influences from Russian games like 'Tysiacha' (1000). The current 'Huutopussi' name and rules stabilized in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 19th Century: Marjapussi is the dominant rural game in Finland.
1920s: Bidding elements are added, creating the 'Huuto' (Bidding) variant.
Present: Highly popular in Southern Finland, particularly among university students.
Tournament Play: National championships are held annually.
history.evolution: The game moved from a simple point-accumulation game to a contract-based game where failing a bid results in heavy penalties.
history.cultural: Regarded as a game of high strategic depth, often associated with mathematical skill and deduction.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: Ace (11), 10 (10), King (4), Queen (3), Jack (2), 9-2 (0). Note: 10 is higher than King.

rules.objective: Be the first partnership to reach 500 points. Points are earned by winning tricks and declaring marriages.
rules.gameplay: 1. Must follow suit. Must overplay (Ylimenopakko): if you can play a higher card than the current winner of the trick, you MUST. 2. Trump: There is no trump until a player who won the previous trick leads a King or Queen and declares a 'Marriage' of that suit. 3. Marriage Values: Spades (40), Clubs (60), Diamonds (80), Hearts (100). Declaring a marriage sets that suit as Trump.
keyRules: Marriage declares trump: Spades 40, Clubs 60, Diamonds 80, Hearts 100

strategy.basic: Priority #1 is capturing Aces and 10s. Since you must overplay, high cards are very powerful for clearing out opponent's trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: The Lead: Winning the contract is crucial because it allows you to lead and declare your strongest marriage as trump immediately.
strategy.advanced: Card Exchange: When exchanging cards with your partner, pass cards that help them complete a marriage or cards that 'void' a suit in your hand so you can use trumps.
tips: The '10' is extremely important; treat it like an Ace in other games.

engine.rankingSystem: Ace (11), 10 (10), King (4), Queen (3), Jack (2), 9-2 (0). Note: 10 is higher than King.
engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck with four suits and thirteen ranks per suit; no jokers. Huutopussi (Finnish) is a point-trick game where card point values (Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, others 0) are collected in tricks; the 10 ranks above the King in play.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each contain thirteen cards. One suit is trump each deal; following suit and playing trump determine trick winner; total card points in the deck are fixed for scoring.
engine.rankDescription: Point values: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, 9-2 zero. For trick play the order is Ace, 10, King, Queen, Jack, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (Ten ranks above King). First to reach the target score (e.g. 52) wins.
engine.dealPattern: Deal 13 cards to each of 4 players

synthesis.shortDescription: A prestigious Finnish partnership trick-taking game with complex bidding, marriage declarations that set trump, and an overplay obligation.

prompts.human: Welcome to Huutopussi, the pinnacle of Finnish card games. Your partnership bids to capture points. If you win the bid, exchange 3 cards with your partner. Then play all 13 tricksâ€”follow suit and remember the overplay rule: if you can play higher, you must. Declare marriages to set trump and earn marriage bonuses. First partnership to 500 points wins.
